sentences.text: This medium-sized pliosaur grew to an adult body length of 7 meters.
Its preserved skull measures 113 centimeters in length, although the back part of the head is missing.
The face is elongated and wide, creating a triangular shape when viewed from above.
Unlike other pliosaurs, the two halves of its jaw were not fused together but separated by 10 millimeters.
Fossils of the front of a plesiosaur snout were found in 2000 on land owned by Jorge Muñoz near Villa de Leyva, Colombia.
Excavation of the nearly complete skeleton occurred between 2004 and 2005.
German paleontologist Oliver Hampe first described the specimen in 2005, classifying it as an indeterminate species of Brachauchenius.
In 2016, researchers including María Páramo and Marcela Gómez-Pérez named the holotype VL17052004-1 as a new genus and species, Stenorhynchosaurus munozi.
The genus name combines Greek words meaning narrow snout lizard.
The specific name munozi honors Jorge Muñoz for finding and reporting the fossil.
It possessed 3 tooth sockets in the premaxilla and 29 in the maxilla; the teeth measured 20 to 45 mm in length and were generally similar in size and shape, making it homodont.
There is no evidence that the animal was consumed by predators or scavengers after death.
Stenorhynchosaurus is classified within the subfamily Brachaucheninae.
The fossils date from the Late Barremian age of the Cretaceous and were found in marine sediments.
The remains were located in the Arcillolitas Abigarradas Member of the Paja Formation, within kaolinitic argillite representing an intertidal marine environment.
